nodes.summary: The map from the labels of the clause-check driver (its own labels and those of the lookup embedded in it) to the host labels sends the driver's label for the answer yes to the cleanup label with answer true, its label for the answer no to the cleanup label with answer false, and every other label $l$ to the host label running the driver at $l$.
nodes.title: Driver labels in the SAT host

nodes.summary: The input alphabet of the SAT host consists of the formula bits, the separator and the witness bits. This partial map sends a witness bit $b$ to $b$ and is undefined on formula bits and on the separator.
nodes.title: Reading a witness bit in the SAT host

nodes.summary: The input alphabet of the SAT host consists of the formula bits, the separator and the witness bits. This partial map sends a formula bit $b$ to $b$ and is undefined on the separator and on witness bits.
nodes.title: Reading a formula bit in the SAT host

nodes.summary: The map from the stacks of the clause-check driver into the host stacks sends each driver stack to the host stack of the same name.
nodes.title: Driver stacks in the SAT host

nodes.summary: The two stacks of the clause-length filter, the token stack $T$ and the side stack $U$, are placed in the host machine by the map that sends $T$ to the host stack $T$ and $U$ to the host stack $U$.
nodes.title: Placement of the filter's stacks in the host

nodes.summary: The stacks of the lookup (the query $T$, the table $B$, the stash $S$, the scratch stacks $A$ and $C$, and the value $V$) are placed in the clause-check driver by the map that sends each of them to the driver stack of the same name.
nodes.title: Placement of the lookup's stacks in the clause-check driver

nodes.summary: The stacks of the tokenizer (the formula bits $X$, the witness bits $W$, the token output $T$, the table output $B$, and the clause and literal counters $CC$ and $LC$) are placed in the host machine by the map that sends each of them to the host stack of the same name.
nodes.title: Placement of the tokenizer's stacks in the host

nodes.summary: Every stack of the clause-check driver has alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$. The driver is embedded in the host machine by sending each of its stacks $T$, $B$, $S$, $A$, $C$, $V$, $P$, $F$ to the host stack of the same name (an injective map) and identifying the alphabet of each with that of its image, which is again $\mathrm{Sym}$, by the identity.
nodes.title: Stack embedding of the clause-check driver into the host

nodes.summary: Both stacks of the clause-length filter have alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$. The filter is embedded in the host machine by sending its stacks $T$ and $U$ to the host stacks of the same names (an injective map) and identifying the alphabet of each with that of its image, which is again $\mathrm{Sym}$, by the identity.
nodes.title: Stack embedding of the clause-length filter into the host

nodes.summary: Every stack of the lookup and of the clause-check driver has alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$. The lookup is embedded in the driver by sending each of its stacks $T$, $B$, $S$, $A$, $C$, $V$ to the driver stack of the same name (an injective map) and identifying the alphabets by the identity of $\mathrm{Sym}$.
nodes.title: Stack embedding of the lookup into the clause-check driver

nodes.summary: Every stack of the tokenizer has alphabet $\mathrm{Sym}$. The tokenizer is embedded in the host machine by sending each of its stacks $X$, $W$, $T$, $B$, $CC$, $LC$ to the host stack of the same name (an injective map) and identifying the alphabet of each with that of its image, which is again $\mathrm{Sym}$, by the identity.
nodes.title: Stack embedding of the tokenizer into the host

nodes.summary: Write $P_0$ for the phase-0 labels, $\Lambda_T$ for the tokenizer labels, $\Lambda_F$ for the labels of the clause-length filter, and $\Lambda_D$ and $\Lambda_L$ for the labels of the clause-check driver and of the lookup. The host labels are in bijection with $P_0 \sqcup \Lambda_T \sqcup \Lambda_F \sqcup (\Lambda_D \sqcup \Lambda_L) \sqcup \mathrm{Bool} \sqcup \mathrm{Bool}$: a phase-0 label $p$, tokenizer label,…
nodes.title: Host labels as a sum type

nodes.summary: The relabelling of the 3-clause filter's labels into the labels of the SAT verifier host sends the filter's exit label *pass* to the start label of the clause-check driver, its exit label *fail* to the cleanup label with answer false, and every other filter label $l$ to the host's copy of $l$ among its filter labels.
nodes.title: Filter exits in the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: A label of the SAT verifier host is one of the following: a phase-0 label; a label of the tokenizer; a label of the 3-clause filter; a label of the clause-check driver or of the lookup embedded in it; a cleanup label carrying an answer bit; or an output label carrying an answer bit.
nodes.title: Labels of the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: For a value $c$ of the 3SAT flag, the host program acts at each host label as follows. Here moving a bit block from one stack to another means repeatedly popping the top symbol of the first stack while it is a bit and pushing it, as a bit token, onto the second, and continuing at the next label once the top is not a bit or the stack is empty.
nodes.title: Program of the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: The relabelling that places the lookup's labels among the driver's labels, whose label set consists of the driver's own labels together with the lookup's labels: the lookup's final label $\mathsf{done}$ goes to the driver's return label $\mathsf{ret}$, and every other lookup label $l$ goes to the copy of $l$ among the lookup's labels.
nodes.title: Lookup labels in the clause-check driver

nodes.summary: The lookup sub-program of the clause-check driver: at each lookup label $l$, it is the lookup program's statement at $l$ with every stack operation moved to the driver's stack of the same name (the lookup's stacks $T$, $B$, $S$, $A$, $C$, $V$) and every jump target relabelled by the lookup-label map, which sends $\mathsf{done}$ to the driver's return label $\mathsf{ret}$ and keeps every other label.
nodes.title: The embedded lookup program

nodes.summary: The five labels of phase 0 of the SAT verifier host: $m_1$ and $m_2$ move the formula bits $x$ off the input (in two passes), $\mathsf{sep}$ drops the separator, and $m_3$ and $m_4$ move the witness bits $w$ (in two passes).
nodes.title: Phase-0 labels of the SAT verifier host

nodes.summary: The map from labels of the tokenizer to labels of the host SAT verifier sends the tokenizer's accepting label to the start label of the embedded clause-length filter, its rejecting label to the cleanup label with answer false, and every other label $l$ to the host label that runs the tokenizer at $l$.
nodes.title: Tokenizer labels in the host machine

nodes.summary: The cleanup loop of the host SAT verifier empties the list of stacks made of the input stack followed by the work stacks $X$, $W$, $T$, $B$, $S$, $A$, $C$, $V$, $P$, $F$, $CC$, $LC$, $X1$, $W1$, $U$, in that order: every host stack except the output stack.
nodes.title: Stacks emptied by the SAT verifier's cleanup
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
